ops.title: Enumerate substitutions joined to a word as a process substitution, and substitutions in redirect targets
ops.description:
`CommandLine.parse` lists a command substitution as a command of its own only when it stands in a word. Two shapes run a program the parse never lists:

- `command -v x ignored<(pkill -f x)`: bash and zsh run `pkill` in the process substitution. `command_subs` (`rust/crates/core/src/command.rs`) scans a word's raw text for `$(…)` and backticks only, so a `<(…)` or `>(…)` joined to other text yields no nested command.
- `command >"/dev/null$(pkill -f x)" -v x`: all four of bash, zsh, sh and dash run `pkill`. `walk_command` builds substitution parts from the assignments and words and never from the redirect targets.

Observed with cc-transcript 14.40.0: `CommandLine.parse(...).occurrences` holds one occurrence for each line, the host command, and no `pkill`. An unquoted heredoc body (`cat <<EOF` with `$(pkill -f x)` on the next line) was not checked and likely has the same gap, since the heredoc is absent from `redirects` and its body from `raw`.

Any command shape is affected, not only `command -v`. captain-hook's session guard reads these occurrences to find calls to `pkill`, `orca` and the like, so a program started this way is invisible to it.

Found by a codex finder pass on PR #54 (the `command -v` lookup fix). That PR does not fix this; it only refuses the lookup reading for both spellings.

ops.text: CommandLine.parse("command -v x ignored<(pkill -f x)") lists a nested pkill command
CommandLine.parse of command >"/dev/null$(pkill -f x)" -v x lists a nested pkill command
A substitution in an unquoted heredoc body is listed or documented as out of scope with a test
